items.title: Karamanlis: We Will Not Ask Turkey’s Permission for Projects in the Aegean
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS – Kostas Karamanlis, the former prime minister of Greece, in his speech at the War Museum in Athens marking the October 28 anniversary, with former Prime Minister Antonis Samaras also present, emphatically raised issues of national interests, rejecting the logic of mutual concessions in Greek-Turkish relations. He pointed out that any acceptance of Turkish authorization for the electricity interconnection would create a precedent with broader consequences for the Aegean. He was sending a clear message that Greece cannot ask Turkey’s permission for the Kasos-Cyprus cable, a warning about a Turkish plan to control the Aegean up to the 25th parallel, and offered sharp criticism of Western allies over their stance toward Ankara and Cyprus. Kostas Karamanlis placed particular emphasis on the Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection, linking Turkish interventions to Ankara’s effort to gain a say even in the implementation of a European project.

items.title: Severe rainfall and flood warnings issued for central Greece and western Turkey
items.summary_raw:
Turkey has been hit by powerful thunderstorms and a fatal tornado this week with more heavy rain expected

Heavy rain and strong winds will continue to affect parts of south-eastern Europe and Turkey over the next few days, as an area of low pressure in the region has allowed for the formation of powerful thunderstorms. During a particularly intense thunderstorm in Antalya, a coastal city in the south-west of Turkey, the formation of a tornado resulted in the deaths of four construction workers on Tuesday. Authorities in Greece and Turkey have released severe rainfall and flooding warnings, as a further 100-150mm (nearly 4-6in) of rain is expected this week in central Greece and western parts of Turkey, with locally higher totals possible.

Travelling eastwards towards south Asia, strong winds and heavy rainfall have swept across the Indian regions of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as Cyclone Arnab made landfall. items.title: Record-breaking high tides spark chaos – and kayak commutes – across California
items.summary_raw:
Seawater surges into low-lying communities from San Diego to San Francisco Bay Area, submerging streets, homes and businesses

Historic high tides have caused chaos up and down the California coast this week, as parts of the state were inundated by record-breaking water levels. Seawater surged into low-lying communities from San Diego to the San Francisco Bay Area, submerging streets, flooding homes and businesses, and jamming important transportation corridors and train routes.

Kayakers and paddle boarders could be seen gliding through typically busy thoroughfares in Marin county, north of San Francisco, on Monday and Tuesday. Several drivers had to be rescued from floating cars in the area, while cyclists who had attempted to cross the temporary lagoon that had formed quickly found themselves waist-deep. Further south, in cities such as Newport Beach, water pounded the emergency infrastructure set up to keep out the swelling sea, which seeped through berms, seawalls and sandbag blockades along the shoreline.

According to Axios, citing a US official, Saudi authorities have asked Trump to give regional mediators additional time to negotiate an agreement with Tehran. Qatar is leading the initiative, supported by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey. One proposal would require Iran to restore UN inspections of its damaged nuclear facilities in exchange for limited sanctions relief and access to frozen Iranian funds. Meanwhile, American and Israeli officials reportedly believe a major bombing campaign could begin after the midterm elections if negotiations collapse. Trump told Axios that the confrontation must be resolved “either through a deal or another way.”  Saudi Arabia’s intervention reflects growing concerns among regional governments about the consequences of another major US-Iran war. A renewed military campaign could trigger Iranian retaliation against American bases, Gulf energy infrastructure, and strategic shipping

items.title: LATEST: With 51.8% of votes counted in Israel's election, neither bloc has a majority.  Netanyahu's bloc has 55 seats, the opposition 49 and the Arab-led parties 16, against the 61…
items.summary_raw: LATEST: With 51.8% of votes counted in Israel's election, neither bloc has a majority.  Netanyahu's bloc has 55 seats, the opposition 49 and the Arab-led parties 16, against the 61 needed to govern.  Likud leads the partial count with 27 seats, ahead of Eisenkot's Yashar (21), the Joint List (12), Bennett's Together (11), and The Democrats and United Torah Judaism (9 each).  The overnight exit-poll updates also moved toward Netanyahu.  Kan 11 now gives his bloc 51 seats, Channel 12 gives it 52 and Channel 13 gives it 51, all up from 50, while the opposition dropped to 49–51.  Channel 14, which is close to Netanyahu, is the only one that now projects him a majority, with 62 seats.  The opposition and both Arab parties together would reach 65.  However, the Joint List has offered only outside support, so any anti-Netanyahu government would have to be a minority government or depend on parties from the other bloc.  Netanyahu, for his part, is 6 seats short in the current count, so the remaining 48% of votes and which small parties clear the 3.25% threshold could decide the outcome.

The government’s plan to fund a multibillion-pound nuclear plant at the Sizewell site in Suffolk represents a “terrible deal” for the UK taxpayer over the rest of the century, according to the government’s spending watchdog.

MPs on the public accounts committee (PAC) have warned the government that the cost of the Sizewell C nuclear reactor could spiral to almost £48bn, leaving bill payers on the hook to provide an extra £9.8bn to construct the plant before 2040 and a further £12bn over its 60-year operating life.

The government-backed Warm Home Loans scheme, which launched on Tuesday, could mean thousands more households are able to access low-carbon energy alternative technologies, thanks to loans ranging from £7,500 to up £35,000.

items.summary_raw:

The statement concerns the recent decision by Libya’s House of Representatives to ratify the 2019 Turkey-Libya memorandum on the delimitation of maritime areas of jurisdiction in the Mediterranean, which, it notes, “raises serious concerns for regional security and stability.” According to the joint statement, the decision also highlights a broader challenge to the international legal order: “the need to ensure that arbitrary bilateral agreements do not undermine established rules of international law or prejudice the rights of third States.”

They impacted the eastern suburbs of Kyiv, striking currently unknown targets. Some of the missiles missed their targets and fell in open areas, due to the low accuracy of modified S-400s.  Ukraine launched two interceptor missiles of an unknown type (not Patriot), but was unable to shoot down any of the 8 ballistic missiles used.

Qatar is reportedly mediating a five-day agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the American naval blockade of Iranian ports. But Tehran’s refusal to make nuclear concessions is complicating negotiations.  According to The New York Times, citing a Gulf state official, Qatari mediators are developing a proposal under which Washington and Tehran would implement a series of reciprocal concessions over five days. Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while the United States would lift its naval blockade on Iranian ports. The main disagreements concern the timing and sequence of those steps, as well as a proposed Iranian nuclear concession that Tehran’s negotiators have rejected. No final agreement has been announced.  The negotiations could offer a path toward reducing military tensions and restoring commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global energy supplies. However, the dispute over which side must act first illustrates the lack of trust between Washington and Tehran. items.title: Nuno Felix RT @BrunoTertrais: Am not sure it's that simple. A NATO operation based on (but not limited to) F35A-B61Mod12 would probably have a high probability to reach targets in …
items.summary_raw: Nuno Felix RT @BrunoTertrais: Am not sure it's that simple. A NATO operation based on (but not limited to) F35A-B61Mod12 would probably have a high probability to reach targets in Russia. And US vs. Fr mission profiles are different.  NATO’s U.S.-led nuclear sharing relies on B-61 gravity nuclear bombs, designed in the 1960s to stop Soviet tank divisions sprinting from East Germany. They have become increasingly obsolete in a modern war—and pose a limited threat to the Russian homeland given advances in Russian air defenses. France’s ASMP-A nuclear-tipped cruise missiles on Rafales, by contrast, are designed to strike Russia’s main cities and have a high chance of reaching their targets, creating an entirely different level of deterrence. The very nature of French nuclear doctrine and its nuclear arsenal makes it in some ways more threatening to Russia, said Nicole Grajewski, an expert on Russia and nuclear affairs at Sciences Po university in Paris. “The B-61 bombs are not instruments for war fighting, they’re pretty much instruments of political assurance,” she said. “The French nuclear arsenal, by contrast, can reach Russia.” @NicoleGrajewski   https://www.wsj.com/world/europe/f

items.title: Iran president says Tehran seeks unity and security among Muslim nations
items.summary_raw:
Iran president says Tehran seeks unity and security among Muslim nations

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has called on Muslim countries to strengthen regional cooperation against what he described as “Israeli aggression” and US-backed efforts to divide the Middle East, as senior Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials met with him in Tehran.

During the meeting with Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Pezeshkian condemned Israeli attacks on Gaza, Lebanon, Iran and other parts of the region.

He said Iran was not seeking nuclear weapons but insisted on its right to pursue peaceful nuclear activities under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

He also criticised what he called “contradictory US policies”

Officials also said President Trump has not made a final decision, appears to lean toward major action, and has backed off at the last moment before. U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) and Pentagon leaders have built a target list covering Iranian energy infrastructure, military sites and nuclear facilities.  Sources told CNN that Iran and the Houthis would likely retaliate immediately against U.S. personnel and facilities in the region but are unlikely to launch preemptive attacks now. items.summary_raw:

Gerapetritis’ presence was of particular significance for the Federation, as this was the first visit to the Stathakion by a serving Foreign Minister of the Greek government in several years. The last Foreign Minister to visit was George Papandreou in 2002. Greece’s chief diplomat attended the event on October 25 and delivered the closing remarks, congratulating the organizers of the event, and noting that he was moved by the presentation.

items.title: Typhoon Champi declared strongest storm of year so far
items.summary_raw:
One dead and 527 injured as winds of up to 185mph hit Taiwan and southern Japan, while Greece issues flood alerts

Typhoon Champi was declared the strongest storm of the year so far after recording sustained winds of 185mph last week. From late Thursday to early Saturday, the typhoon battered Taiwan and Japan’s southern islands. Champi approached the east coast of Taiwan before the centre of the storm turned south along the Yilan County coastline, looping offshore and then tracking northwards away from the island. The storm brought gusts of up to 141mph and 48-hour rainfall totals of more than 620mm to parts of Yilan.

So far, the death toll remains at one, with 527 reported injured. There were widespread power outages, with more than 288,000 houses having no electricity at one point, although most had since been reconnected. Champi has been downgraded to a tropical storm as it rapidly weakens to the south-west of Japan’s mainland on Monday.

items.summary_raw:

The Pentagon's FORTRESS initiative is built to keep major U.S. military bases operating for at least 90 days with no civilian power, outside fuel, water or global supply chains.

Portable nuclear reactors, battery storage and independent microgrids would keep the bases powered. Strategic reserves of ammunition, fuel and spare parts are also planned.

items.title: State Department Calls Announcement of Turkey-Libya Memorandum’s Ratification “Provocative”
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS – The U.S. State Department has described as “provocative” the announcement that the House of Representatives in eastern Libya had ratified the Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum, saying it has heightened tensions in the region and stressing that the U.S. position on the issue has not changed. The new statement, issued in response to a question from Kathimerini, follows a statement on Wednesday, October 21, in which the U.S. State Department encouraged negotiations to resolve maritime disputes, highlighting the economic benefits of a settlement. In its latest response, the department added an explicit condemnation of the announcement of the memorandum’s ratification while reiterating its call for bilateral dialogue between Greece and Turkey. Between the two statements, the Hellenic American Leadership Council (HALC), in a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, had called on the State Department to take a clear public position against the Turkey-Libya memorandum.

items.summary_raw:
The transformation of Europe’s busiest shopping street should be a case study in making cities greener, less congested and more inviting places to live

Sadiq Khan has been trying to pedestrianise Oxford Street since he first became the mayor of London in 2016. On Monday, after numerous setbacks, his plan will finally come to fruition. The busiest stretch of the nation’s famous shopping street will be closed to traffic in a scheme designed to improve the area and make it more attractive to pedestrians. It should be an emblematic case study in making cities greener, less congested, more inviting places to live and visit.

items.title: Türkiye has completed the tender to reconstruct the historic Ani Bridge on its border with Armenia.  The 10th-century Silk Road bridge spans the Arpaçay River, which forms the bord…
items.summary_raw: Türkiye has completed the tender to reconstruct the historic Ani Bridge on its border with Armenia.  The 10th-century Silk Road bridge spans the Arpaçay River, which forms the border between the two countries, at the UNESCO-listed Ani archaeological site in Kars province.   Originally about 80 meters long with a single 31-meter arch, the bridge once served as a customs checkpoint, but its arch collapsed in 1807, leaving only a pier on each bank.   Türkiye and Armenia signed a protocol on the reconstruction in Yerevan in May.   The project is seen as a concrete confidence-building step in the normalization process launched in 2022, as the two countries still have no diplomatic relations and their land border has been closed since 1993.

items.summary_raw:

The foreign minister's schedule includes chairing two high-level open meetings, a meeting with UN Secretary-General António Guterres, and participation in a Security Council meeting on emerging technologies and maritime security, to be chaired by Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis.

items.title: Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant
items.summary_raw:
Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant

Russia’s embassy in Tehran has denied reports that Russian embassy staff and specialists working at the Bushehr nuclear power plant are preparing to leave Iran.

“Neither embassy staff nor Russian specialists at the Bushehr nuclear power plant have any plans to evacuate. Work continues as normal,” the embassy said in a statement, dismissing reports to the contrary as “FAKES”.

Bushehr, Iran’s only operating nuclear power plant, has come under repeated attack during the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Satellite imagery released in July showed damage inside the complex.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, has said that France, Germany and the UK, known as the E3, and Middle Eastern foreign ministers must examine the root causes of military conflict in the region.

In Istanbul, the European foreign ministers underlined the urgent need for diplomacy concerning the US-Israel war on Iran. But Baqaei said diplomacy should not be reduced to a public relations tool and such forums must examine examine the root causes of the conflict.

He condemned the alleged double standards of the E3 regarding their inaction in the face of US and Israeli military aggression against Iran, their comprehensive support for Israel, and their destructive approaches towards Iran’s nuclear issue.

According to General Selçuk Bayraktaroğlu, Chief of the Turkish General Staff, the Turkish Armed Forces aim to produce five million one-way attack drones within the next five years, reaching a total of ten million over ten years. The ambitious plan translates into an average production rate of approximately one million drones annually, reflecting Ankara’s intention to prioritize mass production and the availability of large numbers of relatively inexpensive unmanned weapons.  The scale of Turkey’s proposed production program reflects one of the clearest lessons of the war in Ukraine. Modern warfare increasingly depends not only on sophisticated weapons but also on the ability to manufacture and replace enormous quantities of expendable drones.
